title: Introduce hybrid trace propagation + deferred sampling SDK middleware
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Background:
Redwood currently relies on W3C traceparent for cross-service context and some internal headers for routing/tenant hints. We have gaps: (1) inability to carry lightweight routing/cache/model metadata without adding more headers, (2) inconsistent sampling decisions across services (sample decided at edge and dropped later), and (3) lack of a unified SDK middleware that supports HTTP + gRPC + async frameworks with a single, extensible hook surface.

Goal:
Provide a hybrid propagation format and SDK middleware that: (a) preserves W3C compatibility, (b) carries a compact JSON-safe 'enrichment' token for per-request metadata (route id, model id, cache-hit hint, tenant id), (c) enables deferred sampling (mark-as-candidate header so downstream can decide to promote to sampled), and (d) exposes tracing hooks to allow span enrichment at key lifecycle points (incoming request, after routing decision, before tokenization, after model inference).

Scope / Deliverables:
- New middleware for Node (Express/Fastify), Python (ASGI/Flask), and gRPC interceptors that implement:
  - Transparent W3C traceparent passthrough.
  - An additional header "x-rw-enrich" (base64-encoded compact JSON) carrying enrichment hints.
  - A sampling flag header "x-rw-sample-candidate" with values: "0"/"1"/"deferred".
  - Hook APIs: onRequestStart, onRouteResolved, onModelSelected, onInferenceDone, onRequestEnd.
- SDK-level span enrichment helpers (add_tag, add_event, set_attribute) and guidelines for which attributes are PII-free.
- Backward-compatible fallback: if x-rw-enrich missing, middleware should not drop or override traceparent.
- Tests: unit, integration (cross-service local compose), and high-throughput load test to validate header size/cost.
- Observability: dashboards and alerts for trace sampling ratio by service, dropped-context rate, median header size, and enrichment attribute cardinality.
- Docs: API reference, migration guide for partners, examples for common frameworks.

Design notes / rationale:
- Why hybrid header? Adding custom metadata to traceparent violates the spec; carrying a separate compact header lets us evolve enrichment without breaking third-party tracing. We encode as compact base64 JSON to keep header length reasonable and safe for proxies.
- Deferred sampling: some services (edge gateways) see low signal to decide sampling; allowing downstream services (model-serving pods) to promote a candidate ensures we keep traces for high-cost operations. We must be careful with state: candidate => promotion must propagate back so edge spans become parent of sampled spans or be linked. We'll implement a server-side link: sampled span will include link back to candidate trace id.
- Security and PII: enrichment keys must be scoped to non-sensitive names only. SDK will include sanitizer hooks; default enabled list: route_id, model_version, cache_hint, tenant_id (hashed).

Acceptance criteria:
- Middleware available in Node/Python/gRPC packages with stable APIs and examples.
- End-to-end integration test: request flows through gateway -> router -> model host, with candidate promoted downstream, producing a single linked trace view in the tracing UI.
- No change (or <0.1%) to p95 request latency in the canary service under load test with headers enabled.
- Dashboards showing sampling promotion rate and enrichment attribute cardinality.
- Documentation and migration guide published in the docs site.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge SDK packages behind a feature flag. Publish alpha packages.
2) Deploy middleware to internal staging services, run integration tests.
3) Canary: enable in 5% of gateway traffic for a single region, monitor p95 latency and trace promotion metrics for 48h.
4) Expand to 25% then 100% over a week if metrics stable.
5) Engage partner teams for SDK adoption and provide migration support.

Monitoring and alerts:
- Alert if sampled-to-candidate promotion rate < 0.5% or > 10% (indicates misconfigured sampling logic).
- Alert if dropped-context rate (requests that had traceparent but no downstream spans) increases > 1% baseline.
- Dashboard: per-service sampling ratio, enrichment header size histogram, top 50 enrichment keys and their cardinality to detect high-cardinality attributes.

Testing strategy:
- Unit tests for header parsing/serialization with malformed input.
- Integration via local compose and test harness that spins up Node gateway, router (Python), and model host (gRPC) verifying links and attributes.
- Load test with the trace-candidate flag enabled to measure throughput and header overhead at 1000 req/s for 10 minutes.
- Security fuzz tests for header injection and size overflows.

Dependencies:
- SDK packaging infra (ENG-4821) [dependency placeholder].
- Tracing backend storage changes to support linked spans queries (observability team).
- Console tracing UI change to show promotion links and enrichment attributes (console-frontend).

Migration notes for partners:
- For third-party libraries that only understand traceparent, they will continue to function. Partners that want the enrichment tokens must upgrade to the new SDK middleware. Provide a lightweight server-side adapter to rehydrate x-rw-enrich into older logging pipelines.

Risks and mitigations:
- Header bloat increasing network cost: mitigation — keep enrichment compact, truncate long values, and provide configuration to disable enrichment for low-priority routes.
- Wrongly promoted samples flood tracing backend: mitigation — apply rate-limiting and per-service promotion thresholds.
- PII leakage in enrichment attributes: mitigation — required sanitizer whitelist and review in security step.

Security review required: true
